name: Elon Musk
desc: Controls the empire through votes, not ownership
metric: Owns 42% of SpaceX but controls 82.4% of the votes
facts: Tesla stake worth ~$355B in stock, plus options | SpaceX ~42% stake set to be worth ~$866.5B at the $135 IPO price | Net worth set to pass $1 trillion once SpaceX lists on June 12, 2026
take: The gap is the whole story. He owns far less than he controls. In SpaceX he holds 42% of the money but 82.4% of the votes. Watch whether his voting control keeps climbing even as outside shareholders pour money in.

name: SpaceX
desc: Rockets, Starlink internet, and now AI
facts: Lists Jun 12 2026 on Nasdaq as SPCX at $135 a share | Three segments: Space, Connectivity, AI | Absorbed xAI (Grok) and X in the Feb 2026 merger | Net loss of $4.94B in 2025, and a $4.28B loss in Q1 2026 | Total losses since 2002 top $41.3B
take: This is the cleanest version of the whole map's theme. After the IPO, outside shareholders supply the cash and Elon keeps near-total control. Starlink funds everything else. Watch whether the AI segment's losses ever force that to change.

name: Tesla
desc: Electric cars, batteries, self-driving and robots
facts: ~1.64M vehicles delivered in 2025 | Q1 2026 auto gross margin was 19.2%, up from 16.3% a year earlier | Bought $2B of SpaceX equity in Q1 2026 | Raised 2026 capex guidance to over $25B, and ended Model S and X production in May 2026 | One share, one vote: no super-voting shares
take: Tesla is the one company where Elon's control roughly equals his ownership, about 15%, with no super-voting shares. That makes it the most exposed to a shareholder revolt. The number I watch is energy.

name: The Boring Company
desc: Digs tunnels for underground transit (the Loop)
facts: Runs the Las Vegas Loop tunnel system | ~$905M raised in total | Valuation slipped from $8.6B in 2023
take: The smallest, quietest bet, and the valuation has slipped rather than grown. It matters mostly as contrast: a private company most retail investors will never get access to.

name: Neuralink
desc: Brain implants that let people control devices by thought
facts: N1 implant placed in multiple human patients | ~$1.3B raised since 2016 | No revenue yet
take: The highest-risk, longest-horizon company: real medical progress, no revenue. Locked away from public investors for now. Watch for any pre-IPO chatter.

name: Space
desc: Launch services and spacecraft, the rocket business
facts: Active vehicles: Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Dragon | The loss is driven by Starship R&D | Starship still in test flights
take: The original business now runs at a loss on purpose. Every spare dollar goes into Starship. The question is when Starship starts carrying paying payloads.

name: Connectivity
desc: Starlink internet, plus Starshield for governments
facts: Almost all of this revenue is Starlink | Starshield is the government and defense layer, not broken out separately | About 63% EBITDA margin in 2025 | The cash engine that funds Starship and the AI buildout
take: This is the engine. Starlink is the only segment throwing off real cash, and it bankrolls the rest of SpaceX. If you remember one number from this map, make it this one.

name: AI
desc: Grok AI and the X social network
facts: Formed by folding xAI (Grok) and X into SpaceX in Feb 2026 | Runs the Colossus data centers in Memphis; Colossus 2 came online in Jan 2026 with 555,000 Nvidia GPUs and 1 gigawatt of power | Leases compute to Anthropic at $1.25B a month and Google at about $920M a month, roughly $75B combined | Both compute deals can be cancelled on 90 days notice after end of 2026
take: The newest and most expensive piece. Watch whether Starlink's cash can keep absorbing these losses.

name: Falcon 9
desc: The reusable rocket that funds the space business
facts: 123 of the 165 launches were SpaceX's own Starlink missions | Reusability is the edge, with some boosters past 30 flights | List price is about $74 million per launch | 2025 was the peak; flights ease off as SpaceX shifts to Starship
take: The reliable cash-and-reputation engine of the Space segment.

name: Starship
desc: The giant next-generation rocket aimed at Mars
metric: Flight 12 flew May 22, 2026; Flight 13, the first orbital attempt, is Q3 2026 at the earliest
facts: Version 3 carries 100 tons to orbit, versus about 23 for Falcon 9 | Flight 12 lost one engine but held its trajectory | Flight 13 is the first orbital attempt, pending an FAA review | Built to launch the new Starlink V3 satellites in the second half of 2026
take: The biggest bet inside SpaceX. Watch Flight 13 for the first orbit, and the second half of 2026 for the first commercial payloads.

name: Starlink
desc: Consumer and business satellite internet
metric: 10.3M subscribers as of Q1 2026, up 105% YoY
facts: Revenue per user fell from $99 a month in 2023 to $66 in Q1 2026 | Runs about 9,600 satellites, roughly 65% of all active satellites | Beams direct to phones in 30 countries, with 7.4M devices connected | Tested a $39 a month floor in March 2026, then raised prices $5 to $10 in May 2026 | Churn rate is still not disclosed
take: Subscribers keep climbing while the revenue per user keeps falling. Watch which one sets the trajectory.

name: Starshield
desc: A secure satellite network for defense and government
facts: The national-security version of Starlink | May 2026: cleared by the Pentagon to handle its most sensitive data, IL6 and IL7
take: The quiet, high-margin government layer most retail investors never hear about.

name: Grok
desc: The xAI chatbot, built to rival ChatGPT
metric: Now runs Starlink's support line, resolving 70% of calls before a human
facts: About 117 million people use Grok features | Handles Starlink customer support, with 1 in 5 callers buying on the call | SpaceX has an option to buy the coding tool Cursor, partly for its data to retrain Grok | Grok 5 is training on the Colossus 2 cluster
take: The product SpaceX is spending heavily to rebuild. Watch whether Cursor's data closes the gap with the leading models.

name: X
desc: The social network formerly called Twitter
facts: About 350 million posts a day | Around 550 million monthly users across X and Grok | Bought by Elon in 2022, folded into the AI segment in 2026
take: Now valuable mainly as fuel for Grok rather than as an ad business.

name: Automotive
desc: Designing, building and selling electric vehicles
facts: ~1.64M vehicles delivered in 2025 | Tesla's largest revenue source | Deliveries have flattened
take: Deliveries have flattened. The bull case has quietly shifted from selling more cars to robotaxi and software.

name: Energy
desc: Batteries for homes and the grid (Powerwall, Megapack)
facts: Powerwall for homes, Megapack for grids | Launched Megapack 3 and Megablock | Quarterly revenue is lumpy by project timing
take: The fastest-growing part of Tesla over the full year, even though it dipped last quarter. This is the number I watch.

name: Full Self-Driving
desc: Tesla's self-driving software, the bet on autonomy
metric: Sold per car or as a monthly subscription
facts: Sold as Full Self-Driving (Supervised) | Powers the Robotaxi service | Hardware 3 cars built 2019 to 2023 cannot run unsupervised FSD, confirmed April 2026 | Take rate is rarely disclosed
take: This is where Tesla's valuation story has quietly moved. The cars fund it; the software is the bet.

name: Optimus
desc: Tesla's humanoid robot
metric: Pre-production; Gen 3 reveal due July or August 2026
facts: Used so far for learning and data collection, not yet regular factory work | Chinese makers shipped over 10,000 humanoids in 2025, one priced at $5,900 | The Fremont line that built Model S and X is converting to Optimus, target 1 million a year | Analyst value estimates range widely, from nothing in some base cases to about $93B
take: Mostly optionality today: real ambition, no revenue yet. Watch the Gen 3 reveal and the first production numbers at Q3 earnings.

name: Model 3 & Y
desc: The two mass-market cars that carry Tesla's volume
facts: Among the best-selling EVs in the world | Volume has flattened
take: Volume here has flattened, the heart of the stalled-growth story.

name: Other Vehicles
desc: The rest of the lineup beyond the mass-market cars
metric: Model S, X, Cybertruck and Semi
facts: Lower volume, higher price or niche | Cybertruck ramp has underwhelmed
take: Halo and niche products, not the volume engine.

name: FSD Subscription
desc: Monthly subscription revenue from self-driving
facts: Monthly subscription for FSD (Supervised) | High-margin recurring revenue
take: Tesla rarely broke this out before. Now the subscriber base is disclosed and growing. Real recurring revenue.

name: Robotaxi
desc: The autonomous ride-hailing service
facts: Uses the purpose-built Cybercab | Central to the autonomy case
take: The entire autonomy thesis rests on this scaling. Still very early.

name: TeraFab
desc: The chip factory jointly built by Tesla and SpaceX
facts: A joint chip factory shared by Tesla, SpaceX and xAI | Full breakdown coming in an upcoming video
